overview.title: A quieter historic fabric
overview.p1: Tetouan’s mellah, the historic Jewish quarter, adds another layer to the white city. Lanes feel different from the main souk axes — often quieter, with a residential scale and traces of a community that shaped northern Morocco’s trade and culture.
overview.p2: Visit with curiosity and respect. This is not a theme-park reconstruction; it is part of a living city with memory built into the walls.
overview.p3: Pair a short mellah walk with the main medina rather than treating it as a separate half-day.

q1.question: Is the mellah open to visitors?
q1.answer: Yes — public streets. Private homes remain private.

q2.question: Need a guide?
q2.answer: Helpful for history; not required for a respectful walk-through.

q3.question: How long?
q3.answer: Thirty to sixty minutes for most visitors.

q4.question: Photography?
q4.answer: Be discreet with people and doorways; ask when unsure.

q5.question: Combine with?
q5.answer: Main medina and Place Hassan II the same day.

food.title: Eat nearby

food.p2: The mellah is better as a walking pause than a restaurant hunt.
